**v1.9.1: with `reboost` on, a blade's copies stay in hand for the hit that frees them again.**
- **What was wrong.** With "Boost again after each hit" (`reboost`) on, a hit lets the blades it fits go again. But once a blade had gone both plain and sharpened (with a Sharpened Blade on it), the bot's DiscardSpare threw that blade's other copies away: its both-casts rule didn't look at `reboost`. The simulator has played it that way since v1.9.0, and v1.9.0's notes measured what it cost.
- **What changes in the game.** Only with `reboost` on, as a Hitter (or with the party off), not with Alt+2's pick: those copies now stay in your hand and go again after the next hit the blade fits. debug.log says so once a battle a blade: "storm/blade: its plain and sharpened casts both went - its copies kept in hand: with reboost on, the next hit it fits lets it go again (said once a battle)". A spare Sharpen is still thrown once no blade in hand can take one: it helps (v1.9.0 measured 52.9% for the first deck below against the mobs with both rules off, against 57.0% with only the both-casts rule off, as v1.9.1 plays). Unchanged: `reboost` off (the default); a party's Blader or Healer with the party on, whatever round it plays; Alt+2's pick (left as it was: its blades mostly go on another wizard's plate, whose casts your hit doesn't free); traps (this rule never threw them); `discardspent` (it never runs with `reboost` on).
- **The simulator plays it** (the boss deck pick, the planner, the zone deck) when the AutoFarmer says it keeps them: this AutoFarmer sends one more value with its settings, `reboostkeep:1`, or 0 as a Blader or Healer with the party on and with Alt+2's pick, where the bot still throws them - so those results stay as they were.
- **Measured on the same dice** (2000 battles a cell, each battle on the same seed in v1.9.0 and v1.9.1): a Storm wizard with 3000 health and 60% damage against a 6000-health boss or 3 mobs of 1500 health (2-pip hits of 150-200 and 100-150 that always land), `reboost` on. % won v1.9.0 -> v1.9.1; in brackets, the battles only v1.9.1 won / only v1.9.0 won:
  - 8 Storm Lord + 3 Stormblade + 3 Sharpened Blade: the boss 93.7% -> 94.6% (+58 / -39); 3 mobs 44.5% -> 57.0% (+333 / -84). v1.8.1's simulator won 64.3% against the mobs: it threw the Sharpens away at once. The rest of that gap is the Sharpen played as the bot plays it - held for a blade, and the sharpened cast one more boosting round before a hit.
  - 8 Storm Lord + 6 Stormblade + 6 Storm Trap + 2 Sharpened Blade + 2 Potent Trap: the boss 97.2% -> 97.1% (+2 / -4); 3 mobs 75.3% -> 75.3% (+115 / -115).
  - 4 Storm Lord + 4 Tempest + 3 Stormblade + 3 Storm Trap + 2 Feint + 2 Sharpened Blade + 2 Potent Trap: the boss 96.8% -> 97.2% (+13 / -5); 3 mobs 89.9% -> 90.2% (+43 / -36).
  - 8 Storm Lord + 1 Stormblade + 1 Sharpened Blade, and 10 Thunder Snake + 6 Storm Lord + 4 Sharpened Blade (no blade): the same battles won - no second copy to keep.
  - With `reboost` off (`discardspent` on or off), and with `reboost` on but the value not sent (an older AutoFarmer): every cell the same, battle for battle.
- **Everything else plays exactly as before**, against v1.9.0: 90 random decks without Sharpen or Potent (1890 simulate, 450 planner, 90 team plan and 90 deck pick comparisons, sent the value and not) and 45 random decks with Sharpen, 20 of them with Potent too (1755 simulate, 184 planner as Hitter, Blader and Healer, 23 team plan and 45 deck pick comparisons wherever the bot doesn't change: the value not sent, `reboost` off, or a support), 0 differing.
- **Mixed versions are fine.** An older AutoFarmer with this helper sends no `reboostkeep`: its simulator throws the copies as that bot does, so its results are v1.9.0's. This AutoFarmer with an older helper: the helper ignores the value and plays as before; the zone deck is worked out once more after updating.
- **Not tried in the game yet.** The bot's change was only read, not run against the game: AutoFarmer\LIVE_CHECKS.txt step 2.10 says what to look for and what to send.
- **Updating:** the updater offers this to every install, including ones set up from the v0.7.0 or v0.7.1 zips. Your settings, learned cards and routes are kept. A copy run from the code: git pull.
